item.title: [MAHOUT-1302] SequenceFilesFromMailArchivesTest.testSequential failing
item.description:
SequenceFilesFromMailArchivesTest.testSequential is failing only on ubuntu3 and ubuntu6 Jenkins nodes. Because of that, MahoutQuality and integration job builds either fail or are successful depending on where they get run.

Test fails because it expects entries in chunk-0 SequenceFile to be in specific order, but that order is not guaranteed because of the way the chunk-0 is created/filled - SequenceFilesFromMailArchives traverses input using Java's

File[] java.io.File.listFiles(FileFilter filter)

which does not guarantee order of files/directories.

Unless we want in SequenceFileIterator to guarantee order by sorting, test needs to be changed to verify presence of given files and their content, but not their exact order.

status.description: The issue is considered finished, the resolution is correct. Issues which are not closed can be reopened.

Comment by tdunning on dev mailing list:

I think that deterministicizing (new word alert) the order is a good thing.

I've just committed a change to fix the issue by making order of processing mail archives and (sub)directories deterministic and non-OS specific - first processing files then nested directories, just as expected by SequenceFilesFromMailArchivesTest.testSequential unit test.

I don't like the design of SequenceFilesFromMailArchives - it's using PrefixAdditionFilter which is a FileFilter to traverse the FS tree. That felt unnatural before my change, and feels even more unnatural now after the change.

SUCCESS: Integrated in Mahout-Quality #2213 (See https://builds.apache.org/job/Mahout-Quality/2213/)
MAHOUT-1302 Made order of processing mail archives and (sub)directories deterministic and non-OS specific - first processing files then nested directories, just as expected by unit test (sslavic: rev 1517996)

  • /mahout/trunk/integration/src/main/java/org/apache/mahout/text/SequenceFilesFromMailArchives.java

I don't like the design of SequenceFilesFromMailArchives - it's using PrefixAdditionFilter which is a FileFilter to traverse the FS tree. That felt unnatural before my change, and feels even more unnatural now after the change.

Stevo,

I really don't think that anybody is attached to the current implementation. If you see something that is better, I would very much expect that everybody would applaud and not complain.

Replaced PrefixAdditionFilter java.io.FileFilter usage for walking directory tree with an commons-io DirectoryWalker based implementation.

When Java 7 becomes min JDK for the Mahout project, we should consider using java.nio.file.FileVisitor and java.nio.file.Files.walkFileTree instead, to remove commons-io dependency.

FAILURE: Integrated in Mahout-Quality #2214 (See https://builds.apache.org/job/Mahout-Quality/2214/)
MAHOUT-1302 Replaced PrefixAddition FileFilter with equivalent implementation of commons-io DirectoryWalker, for walking the directory tree (sslavic: rev 1518338)

  • /mahout/trunk/integration/pom.xml
  • /mahout/trunk/integration/src/main/java/org/apache/mahout/text/SequenceFilesFromMailArchives.java

Issue is fixed - was able to reproduce failing test when changing order of dirs and files (dirs first, files after - then it fails), and code in place now guarantees correct order as expected by test (first files then dirs).
Anyway, will close the issue once test passes on either ubuntu-3 or ubuntu-6 node.
